summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of elevated creatinine (2.9 mg/dL) from her baseline of 1.7, detected during a routine transplant clinic visit. She was asymptomatic. Ultrasound revealed mild hydronephrosis and elevated resistive indices, prompting a kidney biopsy which confirmed acute humoral rejection. Treatment included plasmapheresis with a tunneled catheter, high-dose IV steroids tapered to oral prednisone, and four doses of ATG. Due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia, glipizide and Humalog insulin were initiated. Hypertension, worsened by fluid overload and steroids, was managed by increasing labetalol and adding furosemide, while lisinopril was held. Tacrolimus was increased to 6.5 mg twice daily. The patient remained stable, with creatinine plateauing at 2.6 mg/dL. She was discharged home with medication adjustments and close follow-up.
